curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `H M L`; `zt zz zb`; `Ctrl-f`, `Ctrl-b`, `Ctrl-d`, `Ctrl-u`, `Ctrl-e`, `Ctrl-y`; combining a framing command with a stored position
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Move the window rather than the cursor: reach a visible landmark, frame the line you are working on, and travel a long file without losing context
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Center a target line; jump to the last visible row; page through a long file and return; reveal the next rows without moving the cursor
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core through `H M L`, `zt zz zb`, and `Ctrl-d`/`Ctrl-u`. One-row scrolling with `Ctrl-e`/`Ctrl-y` is advanced. All are native Vim; a host editor that embeds Vim may claim the Ctrl chords by default, so check the host you are in

lessons.title: Read the visible window
lessons.objective: Use H, M, and L to reach visible window landmarks.

activities.title: Move to the top, middle, or bottom of the window
activities.body: Press `H`, `M`, or `L` to move to the highest, middle, or lowest visible line. These commands use the current window, not fixed file line numbers.
activities.grammar: H -> visible top; M -> visible middle; L -> visible bottom
activities.contrast: Their destinations change when the viewport changes.

activities.title: Move the view without changing the cursor position
activities.body: Press `zt`, `zz`, or `zb` to show the cursor line at the top, center, or bottom of the window. The cursor stays on the same text.
activities.grammar: zt -> top; zz -> center; zb -> bottom
activities.contrast: These commands change the view, not the text.

lessons.title: Travel by pages
lessons.objective: Move by full and half windows while retaining context.

activities.title: Scroll by a full or half window
activities.body: Press `Ctrl-f` or `Ctrl-b` to move forward or backward by about one window. Press `Ctrl-d` or `Ctrl-u` to move by half a window.
activities.grammar: Ctrl-f / Ctrl-b -> page; Ctrl-d / Ctrl-u -> half-page
activities.contrast: Half pages retain more nearby context.

activities.contrast: Unlike j and k, these commands primarily move the viewport.

lessons.title: Keep your place in a large edit
lessons.objective: Combine marks, viewport movement, and history returns.

activities.title: Choose how you plan to return
activities.body: Use a mark for a place you choose in advance, the jump list for places reached by large moves, the change list for edit locations, and window commands only to change the view.
activities.grammar: planned place -> mark; traveled path -> jump list; edited place -> change list
activities.contrast: The shortest command is not always the clearest recovery strategy.

activities.title: Shuttle between two saved sites
activities.instruction: Visit mark a, then return to mark b.

commandGroups.explanation: Jump to mark a’s exact position.
Jump to mark b’s exact position.

hints: Choose the history or viewport command that preserves your place.
Use backtick-a backtick-b.

feedback.why: Two named marks make planned sites addressable.

activities.title: Choose the right return path
activities.prompt: After several edits and a distant jump, which command most directly revisits the previous edit?
activities.explanation: g; follows edit positions, including edits that were undone.

activities.title: Move the window, keep the place
activities.body: Viewport commands change what you can see without changing where you are. Combined with the marks and history from Unit 9, they let you read a distant part of a file and come straight back.
takeaways: Use H, M, and L when only the visible frame matters.
Use zt, zz, and zb to frame the line you are working on without moving the cursor.
Use Ctrl-d and Ctrl-u to travel; Ctrl-e and Ctrl-y to peek.
Pair a mark with a framing command to return and land somewhere readable.
